himeji_sarashina_itsuki.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. A Feb 2026 reviewer notes the shop raised prices on 1 February 2026, so the figures below (gathered 2021-2025) are likely a little low now.

items.en: Chilled buckwheat noodles on a bamboo mat with cold dipping broth
items.note: The baseline order and the cheapest way to taste the noodles. Pick up a few strands, dip only the bottom third into the tsuyu, and slurp — slurping is normal and pulls the aroma up. Reviewers describe these noodles as on the soft, old-fashioned side rather than sharply firm, and the regular portion as small: say 大盛り (oomori, large) if you are hungry.

items.en: Cold zaru soba served with a plate of tempura on the side
items.note: The upgrade on plain zaru: the tempura arrives separately so it stays crisp. A jalan reviewer describes this shop's tempura as prawn, shishito pepper, sweet potato and carrot in a light crunchy batter. The price is on the board but no source we could read states it.

items.en: Hot soba in dashi broth with tempura sitting in the bowl
items.note: Different from ten-zaru: here the tempura goes into the hot broth and slowly softens, which is the point — the batter drinks up the dashi. A 2022 blogger picked this over the tempura-donburi set because it comes with two prawns instead of one. Price recorded 2022.

items.en: Soba in a thick, mildly spicy Japanese curry-dashi broth
items.note: A shop signature — the Tabelog photo caption reads カレーそば 700円 and ごっつい具だくさん ('loaded with stuff'). One reviewer found it 'a little on the spicy side, and it caught up with the stomach afterwards'. Curry roux is wheat-thickened, so this is the least gluten-friendly thing here. Wear something you don't mind splashing.

items.en: Hot soba with sliced duck in duck-fat-enriched dashi
items.note: The ¥700 a reviewer records was for the 大盛り (large) portion, so the regular is cheaper. That reviewer found the broth lighter and gentler than expected — this is a neighbourhood shop, not a rich Tokyo-style kamo nanban.

items.en: Soba topped with grated mountain yam (tororo), pale and slippery
items.note: Grated nagaimo yam makes a white, viscous, almost foamy topping, usually with a raw egg dropped in the middle — you stir the lot through the noodles. Texture is the whole experience: slippery rather than creamy. Raw yam can make some people's mouths tingle.

items.en: Tempura over rice, glazed with sweet-salty tare
items.note: Reviewers repeatedly say the rice bowls here are as good as the soba — one wrote 'honestly this could be a donburi shop'. A photo caption simply reads 天丼は美味しい ('the tendon is good').

items.en: Chicken and egg simmered in sweet dashi, poured over rice
items.note: The name means 'parent and child' — chicken and egg in one bowl. The egg is left deliberately soft and barely set. Sold alone and inside the ¥750 service lunch.

items.en: Beef or pork with egg over rice — the 'stranger' version of oyako-don
items.note: A Kansai speciality and a good joke to know: because the meat and the egg are not from the same animal, it is the 'stranger bowl' rather than the 'parent-and-child bowl'. Recorded at ¥800 as that day's サービス special.

items.en: Breaded deep-fried pork cutlet simmered with egg over rice
items.note: Panko-crumbed pork, so firmly off any gluten-free list. Frequently appears as the day's service set with a small soba alongside for ¥800.

items.en: Grilled freshwater eel lacquered in sweet soy tare over rice
items.note: The most expensive thing in a shop where almost everything is under ¥1,000. The eel is grilled and repeatedly dipped in a sweet soy glaze, which contains wheat. If there is a small pot of sansho pepper on the table, use it.

items.en: Today's special set — on one recorded day, katsu-don with a small soba
items.note: Written on a board by the door and changing daily; this is what regulars order. A 2025 reviewer chose it over the ¥800 yamakake soba because it bundled a katsu-don AND soba for the same money. Soba can be upgraded to large for +¥50.

items.en: Service lunch — a small rice bowl plus a mini soba
items.note: Recorded in 2025 as oyako-don with mini soba for ¥750 — the best value in the shop. Contents rotate, so point at the board and say kore o kudasai.
Barley-based, so not gluten-free. Recorded at ¥500 in 2022. Cash only, and the shop is run by an elderly couple with a radio playing.

items.en: Bite-sized sweet glutinous rice ball coated in red bean paste
items.note: Fifty yen each, sold singly by the register — the kind of tiny old-shop detail that disappears from Japan a bit more every year. Glutinous rice and azuki bean paste, so usually wheat-free, but made on shared equipment.

himeji_sobakiri_taniguchi.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Course prices are as published by two Himeji news outlets around the 11 June 2025 opening; one Feb 2026 diner reports paying ¥4,730 for a lunch course.

items.en: Basic course: nine small appetisers, tempura, then soba
items.note: This shop does not sell single bowls at lunch — you pick a course, then pick which soba ends it. The nine appetisers arrive together in a box; recorded contents include taro simmered with yuzu, chilled aubergine, a soy-simmered soft egg, steamed chicken, soy-milk okara, walnut-and-apple shira-ae, sesame tofu, shiitake with komatsuna, and simmered daikon. Opened at ¥2,000, now ¥2,200.

items.en: Course built around fish cured in sweet Kyoto white miso and grilled
items.note: Saikyo-yaki means the fish sits a day or more in sweet white miso before grilling, which makes it sweet, dense and caramelised at the edges. A Feb 2026 diner had it as buri (yellowtail). Miso normally contains barley or wheat.

items.en: Top course, built around duck breast seared over charcoal
items.note: The most expensive of the three lunch courses. Duck and soba are a classic Japanese pairing because the rendered fat enriches the noodle broth.

items.en: Plain hot soba in dashi — the no-surcharge choice inside a course
items.note: The soba here is 一九そば (ichikyu soba): 90% buckwheat to 10% wheat, a higher buckwheat ratio than the usual 二八 80/20. The chef says it gives more aroma while keeping the noodle smooth enough to slide.

items.en: Chilled soba covered with paper-thin slices of sudachi citrus
items.note: Sudachi is a small green Japanese citrus, sharper and more herbal than lime. The slices float across the whole surface like coins; you eat them peel and all and the bowl turns fragrant and bitter-fresh. The photogenic order, and the one reviewers keep choosing.

items.en: Soba with grated mountain yam and a raw egg yolk — 'moon-viewing'
items.note: The yolk sitting in the white yam purée is the 'moon' of the name. Stir it all in before eating; it turns the broth silky.
The big splurge, and a sign of what this shop is: a soba maker who learned Japanese haute cuisine from the chef upstairs. Buckwheat and truffle are both earthy aromatics, which is why it works.

items.en: Nine seasonal appetisers presented together in a box
items.note: Eat left to right, lightest first. Recorded contents: taro simmered with yuzu, chilled aubergine, soy-simmered soft egg, steamed chicken, soy-milk okara, walnut-and-apple shira-ae (tofu dressing), sesame tofu, shiitake and komatsuna ohitashi, and furofuki daikon. Rotates with the season.

items.en: Fritter of shredded vegetables, battered with buckwheat flour alone
items.note: Unusual and worth noticing: the shop batters its tempura with buckwheat flour only, no wheat, specifically so the fritter smells of soba. Recorded fillings include spring onion, pumpkin, onion and red pickled ginger. Still fried in shared oil, so 'ask' rather than safe.

items.en: Yellowtail cured in sweet white miso and grilled
items.note: Buri (yellowtail) is a winter fish in Japan, oily and rich; the sweet miso cure firms the flesh and browns it beautifully. Eat it in small pieces between mouthfuls from the appetiser box.
Lunch runs 11:00-15:00 with last order at 14:00, in a room of about 10 tsubo with 8 counter seats and two tables — unhurried, but tight.
Sake is brewed from rice and koji, so it is naturally wheat-free. Ask for おすすめ (osusume, 'the recommendation') — the list changes.
Distilled, so usually tolerated even by coeliacs, but grain-based — flag it if you are strict.
Usually distilled from barley (mugi) or sweet potato (imo); ask which, because the two taste completely different — mugi clean and dry, imo earthy and sweet.

At night the same room becomes a Japanese restaurant called 一意専心 — the staff literally flip the nameplate over on the door. The daytime soba identity and the evening kaiseki identity are two sides of one board.

himeji_gozouroppu.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Priced items come from a Himeji Keizai Shimbun report at opening (July 2024) plus a local blogger's visits; ordering is by tablet and no full price list is published online, so many dishes below have no stated price.

items.en: 'Finishing soba' set — the owner's hand-cut soba as the last course of a drinking session
items.note: This is the reason the shop exists. In Japan you close a night of sake with a carbohydrate 'shime', and here owner Saito-san hand-cuts the soba himself, changing the buckwheat's region of origin with the season. Go before it runs out — it does, and this is not a place for big groups late.

A regular describes the ritual: eat the first mouthful completely plain to catch the aroma, then with salt, then dipped in tsuyu, and finish the last few strands with a raw quail egg stirred in. Two kinds of soba are usually available.
The one repeat customers rave about — cut deliberately fat so you chew rather than slurp, which pushes the buckwheat flavour forward. Ask 'gokubuto arimasu ka?', as it is not always on.

items.en: Cold soba under grated daikon radish
items.note: Grated raw daikon makes the bowl sharp and cooling — the one to order on a hot night. Posted on the shop's own Instagram in March 2026.

items.ja: 五臓六腑セット（お任せ5皿）
items.en: House set of five chef's-choice small dishes
items.note: The easiest order if you cannot read the ordering tablet: five obanzai-style plates chosen by the kitchen. Obanzai are the everyday Kansai home-cooking sides — simmered greens, marinated fish, tofu things.

items.en: Komatsuna greens steeped in cold dashi
items.note: Served chilled, not hot. The greens are blanched then left to soak, so the flavour sits inside the leaf rather than on it. Bonito dashi and soy sauce are both near-certain here.

items.en: Sardines simmered with salted ume plum
items.note: The plum's acidity softens the sardine bones and cuts the oiliness — you can usually eat the fish whole. A classic sake companion.

items.en: Manganji sweet peppers dressed with bonito flakes
items.note: Manganji togarashi is a long, mild Kyoto pepper — sweet, not hot. 'Okaka' is dried bonito shavings, which twitch and curl on the warm vegetable.

items.en: Assorted items simmered in dashi — egg, konnyaku, shirataki, chicken balls
items.note: In Himeji, oden is eaten with 生姜醤油 — ginger soy sauce poured over it — not with the mustard used everywhere else in Japan. Say 'shoga-joyu de' if it does not arrive automatically. A blogger recorded ordering only oden here and still getting change from ¥1,000.

items.en: Compulsory small appetiser that comes with the seat charge
items.note: Not an error on your bill: Japanese izakaya charge a small cover and hand you an appetiser for it. Recorded here as three items — mozuku seaweed in vinegar, a fish cake, and dried nibbles.

items.en: Free-range chicken seared outside, rare in the middle, sliced thin
items.note: Yes, it is close to raw chicken, and yes, it is an ordinary and much-loved thing in Japan when the bird is good. Eaten with ponzu, ginger or garlic.

items.en: Sashimi of the day's fresh fish
items.note: Himeji sits on the Harima Sea, so the fish list is local and changes nightly. The soy sauce it comes with contains wheat.

items.en: Tube-shaped fish cake fried in a green batter flecked with seaweed
items.note: 'Isobe' means seashore — the aonori seaweed in the batter is what gives it the name and the smell. Cheap, salty, and built for beer.

items.en: Miso mixed with toasted buckwheat groats, eaten in scrapes as a drinking snack
items.note: A soba-shop classic: take a tiny smear on a chopstick tip and follow it with sake — it is a seasoning, not a dish. Nutty from the toasted buckwheat.

items.en: Breaded pork cutlet with egg over rice
items.note: An izakaya open until 3am that also makes a proper katsu-don is a specific kind of blessing. Posted on the shop's own Instagram, March 2026. Udon is on the menu too.
The shop names its tasting flights as a joke about world leaders sitting round a table; there is also an オバマ麻生安部セット (Obama-Aso-Abe set) at ¥950. Point at the name and the staff will understand.
The real draw alongside the soba: roughly 150 sakes and 100 shochu, including cult breweries like Juyondai, Aramasa, Jikon and Nabeshima. Ordering is by touchscreen tablet at the seat.
A certified Suntory 神泡 (kamiawa) house, meaning they pour the Premium Malt's with the fine-foam head technique.
The default long drink in Japan — light, very cold, and drunk alongside food rather than after it.
Cheaper and drier than a cocktail; the lemon version is the standard order.

items.en: Fruit liqueurs — plum, yuzu and similar
items.note: Umeshu (plum) is the usual one, sweet and low in alcohol; ask for it ロック (on the rocks) or ソーダ割り (with soda).
Open 18:00 to 3am, closed Sundays, tucked at the back of a building in the Shiocho nightlife block — it takes a moment to find, and that is part of the appeal.

items.ja: パテ・ド・カンパーニュ
items.note: Coarse country terrine of pork and chicken liver, served with watercress. The chef trained in France and is particular about the dice size of the meat and the cooking temperature, which is what separates a good pâté from a dull one. This is the only dish anyone has recorded a price for; the shop posts no menu online, so expect a short handwritten card that changes. Terrines are often bound with breadcrumb, and it is normally eaten with bread.
The signature, worked out over repeated trials by owner Yokomichi Kohei: a salted cream-cheese foam floated on espresso, so the bitterness finishes with a savoury dairy richness. Dairy.
Dairy.
Dairy.
Dairy.

items.ja: メロンクリームソーダ
items.note: Vivid green melon soda with a scoop of vanilla on top — the defining retro Japanese café drink, and the flavour is melon-candy, not real melon. Dairy.

items.en: Hey. mousse with hot espresso poured over
items.note: A cream-cheese mousse that you pour hot espresso onto at the table so the texture and taste shift as you eat. Dairy.

items.en: Croffle — croissant pressed in a waffle iron
items.note: A Korean invention that swept Japanese cafés: laminated croissant dough waffled until the layers caramelise. Wheat, butter.
Cubed bitter coffee jelly with cream — a Japanese café standard rarely seen outside the country. Usually served with dairy cream.
Espresso over ice cream. Note the shop opens Saturdays only, 11:00-22:00, inside the SHARES rental kitchen on Nikaicho arcade — check Instagram before walking over. Dairy.

items.ja: フォアグラとローストビーフ
items.note: The declared number-one seller: low-temperature roast beef under a truffled red-wine sauce, with cheese-enriched mash and foie gras. Red-wine sauces are often flour-thickened.

items.ja: うにとイクラの冷製パスタ
items.romaji: Uni to ikura no reisei pasuta
items.en: Chilled pasta with sea urchin and salmon roe
items.note: Carried over from the group's Kyoto flagship and treated as the house showpiece. Wheat pasta.

items.ja: ホールチーズのクリームパスタ
items.en: Cream pasta finished in a wheel of cheese
items.note: Tossed at the table inside a hollowed wheel of Grana Padano brought in from Italy. Mop the leftover sauce with bread. Wheat and dairy.
Smoked bacon, onsen egg, mentaiko, blue cheese, salmon roe, spinach, mushrooms, lemon. The shop's own tip: soft egg plus bacon turns the cream pasta into carbonara.

items.ja: フレンチマンの肉盛り（シャルキュトリー）
items.note: House-cured sausage, bacon and duck; each also sold singly at ¥880.

items.ja: トリュフクリームのピザ
items.note: Mushroom-concentrated truffle cream base. There is also a pizza of the day. Wheat base.

items.ja: 牛すじ赤ワイン煮込み
items.en: Beef tendon braised in red wine
items.note: The shop points at Burgundy for the pedigree; eat it with bread. Braising liquids are frequently flour-thickened.

items.ja: さかなのパリパリ焼き
items.note: Skin side seared hard, white-wine butter sauce.

items.ja: フレンチマン名物串焼き各種
items.note: The gimmick that defines the place — yakitori-format skewers built with French sauces, each listed with the wine it is meant for. Sauces vary, so check individually.

items.ja: うずらベーコンとプチトマト（バルサミコソース）
items.romaji: Uzura beekon to puchi tomato (barusamiko soosu)
items.en: Quail egg, bacon and cherry tomato skewer, balsamic
items.note: Marked on the menu as the red or white wine skewer — sweet-sour, the easiest one to start with.

items.ja: ゆでタンだいこん（わさびクリームソース）
items.en: Boiled beef tongue and daikon skewer, wasabi cream
items.note: Flagged for white wine; the wasabi hits the nose, which the menu warns about cheerfully. Dairy.

items.ja: ラム肉の香ばしスパイス焼き（クミン&カレー）
items.romaji: Ramu niku no koubashi supaisu yaki (kumin & karee)
items.en: Spiced lamb skewer, cumin and curry
items.note: Red-wine skewer. Curry powder blends sometimes contain wheat.

items.ja: 鶏モモと白ネギ（柚子こしょうサルサソース）
items.romaji: Torimomo to shironegi (yuzu kosho sarusa soosu)
items.en: Chicken thigh and leek skewer, yuzu-pepper salsa
items.note: Paired with sparkling on the menu. Yuzu kosho is a fermented citrus-chilli paste, salty and fierce.

items.ja: 鶏レバー赤ワインタレ焼（シナモン風味）
items.en: Chicken liver skewer, cinnamon red-wine glaze
items.note: The menu's own verdict: 'this is a red wine situation'.

items.ja: つくね（ブルーチーズソース）
items.en: Chicken meatball skewer, blue cheese sauce
items.note: Tsukune is minced chicken formed on the skewer; usually bound with starch or breadcrumb. Dairy.

items.ja: ホタテのガーリックパン粉焼き
items.en: Scallop skewer baked with garlic breadcrumbs
items.note: Panko — wheat.

items.en: Prawn skewer wrapped in kadaif pastry
items.note: Kadaif is shredded filo — it fries into a bird's nest of crunch. Wheat.
Listed on the menu as the answer when you cannot decide.
Cheapest thing on the menu. French bistro standard: carrot in lemon-mustard dressing. Dressing may contain honey or dairy.

items.ja: ウフマヨポテトサラダ
items.note: The Parisian boiled-egg-and-mayonnaise classic crossed with Japanese potato salad. Egg.
Coarse country pork terrine, cut thick.

items.ja: カニみそクリームコロッケ
items.note: Kanimiso is the rich brown paste inside a crab's shell — intense, and much loved in Japan. Panko and roux.

items.ja: フレンチマンの卵焼き（釜揚げしらす）
items.note: A bacon-and-spinach version is ¥858. Tamagoyaki is normally seasoned with dashi, soy and mirin.

items.ja: アヒージョ バゲット付（シュリンプ）
items.note: Garlic-and-oil casserole, served bubbling; a camembert version is ¥968. Baguette is wheat — the oil itself is fine.

items.ja: ムール貝白ワイン蒸し
items.note: Moules marinière, the shop's cheapest full sharing dish.
Dairy.

items.ja: ブラックペッパーチーズケーキ
items.note: Pepper cuts the sweetness — designed to be eaten with the wine you already have.

items.ja: シュラブサワー（レモンと桃／りんご／ブラッドオレンジ）
items.en: Shrub sour — fruit vinegar and craft gin
items.note: Fruit vinegar plus craft gin and soda; sharp rather than sweet.

items.ja: JJK（ジャスミン焼酎の紅茶割り）
items.en: Jasmine shochu with unsweetened black tea
items.note: For people who dislike carbonation — no soda, no sugar. Base shochu type unstated, so ask if coeliac.

items.ja: コーヒーとオレンジトニック
items.note: House brandy steeped with orange and coffee.

himeji_tedauchi_sobadokoro_yaem.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. This shop has raised prices repeatedly (the katsudon set went ¥1,250 → ¥1,350 → ¥1,580 across 2023-2026), so the figures below are the most recent reported. Cash only.

items.en: The house set: mini soba, mixed rice, tempura, sashimi, a fried main and dessert
items.note: The order to make. One 2025 tray held kayaku-gohan (rice steamed with daikon, carrot and konnyaku), a mini soba, oyster fry, tempura (pumpkin, pepper, prawn, red ginger), sashimi (prawn, salmon, octopus, scallop) and buckwheat-tea warabi mochi. Reported at ¥1,500 in Sept 2025 and ¥1,680 in 2026. You choose hot or cold soba, and white rice or the mixed rice.

items.en: Pork cutlet and egg rice bowl with soba and sides
items.note: The most-repeated order in the reviews after the house set. Panko-crumbed pork simmered with onion and egg. Recorded at ¥1,250 in 2023, ¥1,350 in 2025, ¥1,580 in 2026.

items.en: Tempura set with soba and rice
items.note: Reviewers consistently say the tempura arrives straight from the fryer and there is a lot of it — 'you get full on the tempura alone'.

items.en: Cold zaru soba paired with a small tempura rice bowl
items.note: The classic Japanese lunch shape: cold noodles plus a small hot rice bowl, so you get both temperatures. ¥1,100 in 2022, ¥1,380 by 2025. Warabi mochi is included.

items.en: Conger eel over rice, with soba on the side
items.note: Anago — saltwater conger eel — is the Himeji castle-town speciality, lighter and more delicate than the freshwater unagi you meet elsewhere in Japan. If you eat one local thing here, make it the anago. It also turns up as 穴子天そば (anago tempura on soba) and 穴子天丼 on the daily board.

items.en: Soba with prawn and scallop tempura, hot or cold
items.note: You will be asked あたたかい (warm) or つめたい (cold) — cold keeps the tempura crisp, warm lets it soak up dashi. Recorded January 2025.

items.en: Cold soba under grated daikon radish
items.note: A clean, sharp bowl for a hot Himeji afternoon; the raw daikon cuts the sweetness of the tsuyu. Recorded 2025.

items.en: Cold zaru soba with tempura served alongside
items.note: One reviewer notes the chicken tempura arrives a minute after the rest because it is fried to order — a good sign, not a mistake.
Best cold. A user-submitted menu listing puts it around ¥1,000. Slippery, mild, and traditionally regarded as a stamina food.

items.en: Soba in thick Japanese curry broth
items.note: Also sold as カレーうどん with fat wheat udon noodles instead. The roux is wheat-thickened, and it splashes.

items.en: Hot soba topped with a sheet of sweet simmered fried tofu
items.note: 'Kitsune' means fox — folklore says foxes love fried tofu. The aburaage is simmered in sweet soy until soaked and floppy; bite it and it releases broth. The cheapest comfort order, also available as きつねうどん.

items.en: Soba with tempura and grated daikon together
items.note: The daikon keeps the tempura from feeling heavy — the reason this combination exists. Also offered as 天おろしうどん.

items.en: Assorted raw fish over rice, with soba, tempura and dessert
items.note: A reviewer calls this the 'luxurious set' — sashimi bowl plus soba plus tempura plus warabi mochi — and warns you will be extremely full. Mini versions exist (ミニマグロ山かけ丼, ミニサーモン山かけ丼) if you want less rice.

items.en: Chicken-and-egg rice bowl set with a choice of hot or cold soba
items.note: Photographed on Tabelog as 親子丼定食（冷たい蕎麦）— with the cold soba option. The egg is left glossy and barely set.
Adding it turns the soba into a two-tier stacked box. Worth it if you are hungry — the mini soba inside a set is genuinely mini.

items.en: Wobbly bracken-starch jelly flavoured with roasted buckwheat tea
items.note: The shop's signature ending, included with the set meals and made in-house since it opened in 2017. Cool, barely sweet, dusted with kinako soybean flour, and it dissolves rather than chews. A takeaway box of eight is ¥880.
From the shop's own Instagram. Add ¥2,200 for 飲み放題 (nomihodai, all-you-can-drink). Reserve ahead; there is also an おまかせコース from ¥3,500.

items.en: Today's recommendations, chalked on a blackboard
items.note: Read this before you commit — recorded examples include an anago tempura don and a mini sudachi-citrus soba with warabi mochi. The owner trained in soba from the age of 18 and cuts it behind a big glass window facing the Omizosuji arcade, so you can watch before you sit down. Open 11:00-20:30 straight through, closed Mondays, and it shuts early when the soba runs out. The noodles are compared to Izushi soba: firm, with real bite.

The default order if you can't read the pot. The owner picks five and will work around anything you dislike — say what you can't eat when you sit down. Dashi is rausu kombu, hana-katsuo and tuna-bushi, kept deliberately light on salt; Himeji-style, you grate your own ginger at the table and mix it with soy from Tatsuno (the shop uses Ogi-ichi) rather than using mustard.

items.ja: おでん8品に牛すじ付き
items.en: Eight oden pieces plus beef tendon
items.note: The full sit-down set at a seven-seat counter. Beef tendon is the shop's showpiece, so it is separated out of the count.
The add-on for people still hungry — udon dropped into the same oden broth as a finisher.
Prepped hard to remove any gaminess, then simmered with kombu and ginger in the oden broth. The signature single item here.
Bitter leafy green, briefly dipped rather than stewed. Shaved yuzu peel is added to soften the bitter edge — an unusual touch for oden.
The most-ordered item in the pot: cut thick and cooked until the dashi has soaked all the way to the core. Broth contains soy sauce and bonito.
A ground-fish-and-tofu dumpling that is deep-fried then simmered — a Kanto oden staple that surprises Kansai diners. Fish cake usually contains wheat starch, so ask.

The whole point of the place: the owner spent 15-17 years behind a British pub bar in Himeji and pairs gin with oden. Ki No Bi from Kyoto (gyokuro and yuzu botanicals) is the house recommendation for Japanese food; Benizakura Distillery's gin, built on kombu and daikon, is poured as a closer.
Covers the roughly 40 craft gins. Beer is included in most such plans, so not gluten-free overall.
Barley beer — contains gluten.
Rice, water and koji only.
Seven counter seats only, so reserve two days ahead by Instagram DM.

About 30 kinds in an L-shaped counter wrapped around the pot, eight seats only. There is a written menu, but the okami's advice — repeated by regulars — is to look into the pot and point, because what is actually in it changes daily. Order four or five on one big plate, the local way, or ask for a small bowl if you would rather go slowly. No mustard: Himeji eats oden with ginger soy sauce.
Arrives unasked and is charged for; normal practice at Japanese drinking places.
Slim, pungent pickled shallots from Okinawa — crunchy, sharp, usually served with bonito flakes and soy.
Soy-milk film, silky and light — a favourite closer.
Charred outside, sweet and collapsing inside once it has sat in the dashi.
Jade-green nuts, slightly bitter and faintly resinous. Autumn item; usually just salted.
Served with proper Japanese karashi mustard, which is sharper than it looks. Wheat wrapper.
Minced oily fish bound with ginger; softer and more savoury than the smooth white fish cakes.
Spring item — crisp at the base, tender at the tip.

items.ja: ちりめんじゃこおろし
items.en: Tiny dried sardines with grated daikon
items.note: The standard palate-cleanser between rounds of sake — salty whitebait on cold grated radish, splashed with soy or ponzu.
From Tokushima across the strait; drunk here warmed.
Awaji Island brewery, known for rich yamahai-style sake that stands up to oden broth.
Contains barley.

The signature and the reason people queue: a roughly 300g panko chicken cutlet larger than your hand, sitting on about 400g of fried rice studded with the shop's own char siu, plus a mountain of cabbage and salad pasta, all under house-made tartare sauce. Everything from the tartare to the dressings is made in the shop and the cutlets are fried to order. Panko and wheat.

Roughly double the signature dish and about 2kg in total: chicken cutlet, fried rice, three pieces of karaage, napolitan spaghetti, salad and potato salad on a banquet platter. Treated locally as a challenge, though the shop says plenty of people finish it. Wheat throughout.

Nothing to do with Sicily — it is a speciality of Saga in Kyushu: sweet-salty grilled beef and raw salad piled on rice with mayonnaise, here with a soft egg on top and a house sauce given a little doubanjiang heat. Soy and doubanjiang contain wheat; egg in the mayonnaise.

items.ja: 播州百日鶏のささみ刺し
items.en: Raw chicken breast sashimi, Banshu hyakunichi chicken
items.note: From 16:00 the shop becomes a bistro called YORU NO MARUMASA, lights down, wine on. This is raw local chicken fillet — a Kansai izakaya habit that startles most visitors. Banshu hyakunichi-dori is the Harima region's own slow-grown bird. Served with soy or ponzu.
Steamed pork dumplings made in-house. Wheat wrapper.

items.ja: トリュフ香るユッケブルスケッタ
items.note: Korean-style seasoned raw beef on toasted bread with truffle — the kind of genre-blind cooking the evening menu specialises in. Wheat bread; yukke seasoning contains soy.

items.ja: 国産牛もも肉のステーキ
items.note: Sauces at Japanese steak counters usually contain soy.

Roughly 30-35 kinds, mostly local ingredients. The dashi is the draw: Rishiri kombu simmered about an hour, then bonito flakes passed through for barely a minute. Ginger soy sauce here is cut with the oden broth itself, so it is milder than the neat shoga-joyu you get elsewhere in Himeji. Broth contains soy sauce and bonito.
One of the items kept permanently in the pot rather than added to order.
From Nishimoto Tofu-ten, a local maker. Springy, dashi-soaked; ginger soy tightens it up.
Also from Nishimoto Tofu-ten — firm tofu scorched on both faces so it holds together in the broth.

items.en: Rice cake in a fried tofu pouch
items.note: A drawstring pouch of abura-age tied with kanpyo, molten mochi inside. The mochi comes from Kineya.
Holds a lot of broth; one of the standing items.
A Shiga speciality, dyed rust-red with iron oxide — startling to look at, tastes like ordinary konjac. A standing oddity in this pot.

items.en: Burdock root in fried fish cake
items.note: Added to the pot only once you order, so it stays crisp-edged. Fish cake contains wheat.
Dropped in briefly — regulars order it for the texture and to taste the broth cleanly.
The silky film lifted off simmering soy milk. Delicate, so it goes in last; a common way to finish here.
Chewy, mochi-like; it is literally wheat gluten, so avoid entirely if coeliac.

items.en: Bracken shoots in a fried tofu roll
items.note: Shinoda means wrapped in abura-age; here it hides warabi (bracken fern shoots). Rare enough that regulars order it every visit.
Bought from Tonraishun, a long-standing local Chinese shop, then put in the oden pot. Wheat wrapper.
Landed in the Harima Sea just south of the city — a standing item, priced by the day's market.
The house original, invented by the previous okami. A winter-only oddity that works because the bacon fat enriches the dashi.
Not an oden item — served as a side dish. Anago from the Seto Inland Sea is the Himeji castle-town speciality; price follows the market. Glazes normally contain soy and mirin.
A small charged appetiser that arrives automatically, standard at Japanese drinking places. Usually topped with bonito flakes and soy.
The okami keeps a dozen-plus bottles rotating, built on Hyogo names — Tatsuriki and Seppikosan — plus her own favourites such as Keigetsu Ginnoyume, Itaru and Kokuryu.

items.ja: 【昼の部】おまかせベーシック
items.note: Lunch starts all together at 12:00, so you book a seat at a sitting, not a time. Seasonal nigiri, creative sushi and sashimi. A cheaper ¥3,850 basic sushi course also appears on the booking page.

items.ja: 【昼の部】おまかせスペシャル
items.note: The upgraded lunch, built on more tightly selected fish; a ¥6,600 'tokusen' sushi course sits between the two on the reservation page.
18:00 seating, kitchen stops at 20:00. The theme changes every month, so the course is genuinely different across the year. Book ahead; this is a counter restaurant.

items.ja: ペアリング 日本酒[六種類]
items.note: Matched to the course. Sake is rice-based and gluten-free.

items.ja: ペアリング ワイン[六種類]
items.note: Some wines are fined with animal products.

items.ja: 今夜のおばんざい盛り合わせ
items.note: From 21:00 the same chef reopens the room as a late-night counter — the 'Iida late-night diner' — with everything a la carte and very cheap for the cooking. This is the best-value way into the place. Obanzai are Kyoto-style everyday vegetable dishes, dressed with dashi and soy.
Whatever came in that day — ask the counter. Soy sauce contains wheat.
A rolled omelette soaked with dashi rather than sweetened — the standard test of a Japanese kitchen. Contains soy and bonito.

items.en: Salt-grilled sweetfish from the Ibo River
items.note: Ayu from the river that runs down to Himeji — eaten whole, guts included, which give it a clean bitterness. Summer only. Just salt and fire.

items.en: Pike conger and onion bound in egg
items.note: Hamo is the bony summer eel of the Inland Sea, painstakingly bone-cut before cooking — the great Kansai summer fish. Simmered in dashi-soy, then set with beaten egg.

items.ja: 鱧と雲丹のハーモニー
items.note: The luxury version of the summer hamo dish.
Winter delicacy — grilled until the outside blisters and the inside turns to hot cream. The most prized of all shirako.
Seared outside, raw inside. Hyogo is Kobe beef country. Ponzu contains soy sauce.
Remarkably cheap for wagyu because it is a late-night a la carte plate. Sauce may contain soy.
Freshwater eel lacquered with a sweet soy tare and grilled over charcoal. Tare contains wheat.

items.ja: 鰻の天麩羅 玉葱醤油
items.note: Tempura batter is wheat.

items.en: Grilled spring onion with ginger soy
items.note: Ginger soy sauce is the Himeji signature dip, borrowed here for grilled leeks.
Sake, clam, lid on. Nothing else needed.
Whole young ayu, crisp enough to eat head and all. Dusted in wheat flour or starch.
Awaji Island onions are famously sweet — in tempura they turn almost jammy. Wheat batter, and tempura dip contains dashi and soy.
The chef cuts his own soba — unusual for a sushi counter. Japanese soba is nearly always cut with wheat flour, and the dipping broth contains soy and bonito.

items.en: Sea bream in hot somen broth
items.note: Nyumen is somen served hot in dashi — the Nara-and-Harima way to end a night. Wheat noodles.

items.ja: 茶漬け（梅・海苔・山葵）
items.en: Rice in green tea — pickled plum, seaweed or wasabi
items.note: Hot tea or dashi poured over rice; the traditional last thing you eat before going home. Broth normally contains soy and bonito.
Brushed with soy and charred on the grill.
Panko-crumbed minced beef and pork, deep-fried — a comfort-food joke on an otherwise refined menu. Wheat.

items.ja: 飯田の溺愛のぬかづけ
items.note: Vegetables fermented in a rice-bran bed — sour, funky, and a house obsession. Rice bran, not wheat.

himeji_juwari_soba_daidai.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The four-item list below is a diner's verbatim transcription of the shop's standing pavement menu board, recorded June 2022; the shop posts no menu online, so prices may have risen since.

items.en: Chilled 100% buckwheat noodles on a mat, with cold dipping broth
items.note: The default order and the whole point of the shop. These are 十割 (juwari) noodles — buckwheat flour and water, no wheat binder at all, which usually makes soba fragile, but a press extruder here produces a surprisingly springy thin noodle. The owner will tell you to try the first strands with the wasabi salt rather than the tsuyu; do that, then switch to the broth. The dough is mixed and extruded to order in front of you, so allow real waiting time — this is not a quick lunch.

items.en: Cold juwari soba topped with grated daikon radish
items.note: Grated raw daikon adds a peppery, watery sharpness that suits a 100%-buckwheat noodle, since there is no wheat sweetness competing with it.

items.en: Cold soba with grated daikon and Nanko-ume salted plum
items.note: Nanko-ume is the premium Wakayama plum cultivar — big, soft-fleshed, intensely sour and salty. Break it up and drag it through the noodles a little at a time; a whole mouthful at once is startling. The most refreshing thing on the board in summer.

items.en: Cold soba under grated mountain yam
items.note: Sticky white yam purée coats every strand — a completely different mouthfeel from the plain zaru, closer to slippery than creamy. Stir it through before eating.
Reviewers say the standard portion is already substantial for juwari soba, so only add this if you are genuinely hungry.

items.ja: セット（ご飯・小鉢・デザート）
items.en: Set upgrade: a small rice, a vegetable side and a dessert
items.note: Extraordinary value for ¥200. Recorded contents on one visit: takikomi-gohan studded with tiny shrimp, a choice of salt-boiled asparagus or kombu tsukudani, and coffee jelly. Contents rotate.

items.en: Himeji-style oden — dashi-simmered items eaten with ginger soy sauce
items.note: There is an oden pot at one end of the counter. The Himeji rule is 生姜醤油 (shoga-joyu): you pour ginger-infused soy sauce over the pieces instead of dabbing them with the mustard used in Tokyo and Osaka. Ordering a couple alongside the soba is exactly what locals do. No prices published — ask at the counter. Note the shop is soba at lunch only (11:00-15:00, last order 14:00) and turns into cafe-bar Orange from 15:00.

Ekisoba is Himeji's great culinary oddity and this shop, at the castle's foot inside a samurai-residence-style building, is run by Maneki Foods who invented it. In 1949, with wheat flour rationed, they used yellow Chinese-style noodles made with kansui alkaline water and served them in Japanese bonito-kombu dashi — a deliberate mismatch that stuck. The result is not soba at all: springy yellow noodles, clear light broth, a soft tempura fritter dissolving into it. Prices shown are Maneki's standard ekisoba prices; the castle-front branch may charge more. Wheat noodles and batter.

items.ja: ごぼう磯部揚げえきそば
items.note: Confirmed being served at this castle-front branch. A generous burdock fritter bound with nori — the root vegetable suits the dashi better than the plain tempura. Wheat.
Kitsune means a sheet of abura-age simmered in sugar and soy — named for the fox said to love it. A double portion is ¥570. Wheat noodles; dashi contains bonito.
The most substantial version. Wheat.
Japanese curry roux loosened with the dashi — thick, mild and startling over Chinese noodles. Roux is flour-based.
For anyone who wants ordinary noodles instead of the yellow ones. Wheat.
Listed as 'wa-soba' precisely because ekisoba is not soba. Japanese soba is cut with wheat flour.

items.ja: 持ち帰りえきそば（2人前）
items.note: The obvious edible souvenir. A dried-noodle 3-serving box is ¥1,280. Wheat.

items.ja: バタリープレーンスコーン
items.note: The bestseller since opening and the one to try first. These are New York-style scones, not English ones: over 5cm thick, heavy in the hand, made with Hokkaido flour and Yotsuba cultured butter, and deliberately under-mixed so the crumb stays sandy and shatters rather than crumbling softly. Wheat and dairy.

items.ja: リッチクリームスコーン
items.note: Made with double cream, so it is softer and milkier than the plain, with a sugar crust on top. Wheat and dairy.

items.ja: アールグレイとくるみのスコーン
items.note: The owner's own pick — tea leaves worked through the dough with walnut pieces. Wheat, dairy, nuts.

items.ja: チョコチップスコーン
items.note: Cut as a triangle rather than a round, which is the New York tell. Wheat and dairy.

Topped with three whole candied chestnuts. The shop runs about 20 scone varieties at a time with daily rotations, plus month-by-month specials — Halloween cookies in October, stollen and snowball cookies in December. Wheat and dairy.

items.ja: チョコバナナマフィン
items.note: Muffins here also clear 5cm, with a thick crumble lid that is the shop's signature. About five kinds daily. Wheat, dairy, egg.
Contents chosen by the shop; sold through the official online store rather than over the counter. Wheat and dairy.

The only thing served at lunch — there is no menu to choose from. Seasonal home-style Japanese cooking with everything made in-house down to the pickles and the salad dressing. The room's large windows look straight at the Himeji Castle keep and moat, which is the real reason to come. Orders taken until 14:00, earlier if ingredients run out; phone reservation only and cash only. Japanese home cooking runs on dashi and soy sauce, so expect both.

'Ate' is Kansai slang for something to drink with. Contents change nightly and there is a separate whiteboard of daily specials next to the printed menu. The shop opened recently on the first floor above the Omizosuji arcade; drinks are cheap and the sake list is unusually long for the price band.
Yam cut into matchsticks and eaten raw — crisp, faintly slimy, very clean. Usually served with nori and a soy dip.

items.ja: 日本酒 奥播磨 純米
items.note: Brewed by Shimomura Shuzo in the hills north of Himeji — the most respected of the local Banshu labels, full-bodied and good warmed.
A dry Kochi sake named after Sakamoto Ryoma's eight-point plan; bone-dry, a standard izakaya benchmark.
There is a wall of dagashi — cheap Japanese corner-shop snacks — hung up as bar food. Order one when you want to keep drinking without eating properly. Wheat-based.
Contains barley.

The castle-town speciality: thick fillets of Seto Inland Sea conger, grilled with a sweet glaze and laid over rice. Softer and cleaner-tasting than freshwater unagi. Price is from a 2016 visit and was quoted before tax, so expect more now. Tare glaze contains soy sauce and therefore wheat.

items.en: Beef tendon and konjac stew over rice
items.note: Bokkake is the Nagata (Kobe) speciality — beef sinew simmered soft and sweet with konjac. Comes with miso soup and pickles. 2016 price, quoted before tax.

The closest place to the castle gate where you can eat Himeji oden as a proper lunch set rather than as drinking food. Simmered in Kansai-style light dashi and eaten with ginger soy sauce poured over, not mustard — that dip is the entire definition of 'Himeji oden'.

items.en: Pork cutlet on rice with demi-glace
items.note: Katsumeshi is a Kakogawa invention just down the line: a beef or pork cutlet laid on rice, coated in a dark demi-glace sauce and eaten with chopsticks, with boiled cabbage on the side. Panko and flour-thickened sauce.
Japan's best-known somen brand, hand-stretched in Tatsuno just west of Himeji since the 1400s. Hair-thin wheat noodles, normally served ice-cold with dipping broth in summer. Wheat.

items.ja: ミヨシのおまかせ3品セット
items.note: You cannot choose the three — that is the point. Past sets have run prawn fritters, simmered chicken liver, and dried persimmon with dried fruit and mascarpone, which tells you how wide the kitchen ranges. The best single order if the menu defeats you. The shop is booked out most nights, so call ahead.
Not the Chinese standard — this version hides daikon and aubergine in the wrapper. Wheat wrapper.

items.ja: マグロのタルタルのり天乗せ
items.en: Tuna tartare topped with fried seaweed
items.note: Chopped raw tuna under a sheet of nori fried in batter — the crunch on top is the whole idea. Batter is wheat.
Deep-fried aubergine under sticky grated mountain yam; usually finished with dashi-soy.

items.ja: アンチョビポテトフライ
items.note: Chips tossed in anchovy — the fryer is shared with battered items, so ask if it matters.
Japanese hamburg: a seasoned minced-meat patty, no bun. Almost always bound with breadcrumbs.

items.ja: スパニッシュオムレツ
items.note: Potato and egg, cut into wedges — a fixture of the creative side of this menu.

items.ja: おとなのレーズンバター
items.note: Cold slabs of butter studded with liquor-soaked raisins, eaten in slivers with spirits. A classic Showa-era bar snack. Dairy.

items.ja: 季節の果物 生ハム巻き
items.note: Whatever fruit is in season stands in for the melon.

items.ja: 刺身（マグロの醤油だれ、刻み海苔）
items.en: Sashimi — tuna in sweet soy with shredded nori
items.note: The quickest thing to arrive when the kitchen is buried, which it usually is. Sweet soy marinade contains wheat.
This kitchen's version has beans in it. Doubanjiang and most soy seasonings contain wheat.
Fried hard so the edges shatter; tiny pink shrimp through the batter. Wheat batter.

items.ja: ホタルイカのネギ焼き
items.note: Negiyaki is the Kansai cousin of okonomiyaki, loaded with spring onion instead of cabbage. Firefly squid are a spring delicacy, whole and briny. Wheat batter.
Whipped prawn paste, deep-fried light. Appears in the omakase three-plate set. Wheat.
Braised in sweet soy with ginger. Soy sauce contains wheat.

items.ja: 干柿とドライフルーツのマスカルポーネ
items.en: Dried persimmon and dried fruit with mascarpone
items.note: Dessert-adjacent but served as a drinking plate. Dried persimmon is intensely sweet and jammy. Dairy.
Sweetened and diluted — pitched at people who do not like beer. Order the draught instead if you do.

items.ja: 漬けこみチューハイ みかん
items.note: Fruit steeped in shochu in-house, then topped with soda. Distilled shochu itself is gluten-free, but barley shochu is made from barley — ask if coeliac.
The default Japanese highball. Grain whisky — usually considered safe once distilled, but coeliacs often avoid it.
Made from barley; ask for an imo (sweet potato) or kome (rice) shochu instead if avoiding gluten.

Lunch is this and nothing else — no choosing. One recorded set was fried chicken as the main, plus sea bream sashimi, chawanmushi and a simmered side. Weekdays only, roughly 11:30-14:00. Unusually complete for the money.
Marinated in soy and ginger, dusted and fried — the shop's is singled out as worth ordering on its own in the evening. Wheat or wheat-containing marinade.

items.ja: ささみと明太子の包み揚げ
items.en: Chicken breast and spicy cod roe parcels, deep-fried
items.note: Lean chicken fillet wrapped around chilli-cured pollock roe and fried. The house favourite — it sells out. Wheat wrapper.
Cod sperm sacs — creamy, custard-like, and a genuine winter delicacy rather than a dare. Ponzu contains soy sauce.
The shop's most-ordered small plate. Japanese versions are mashed rougher and dressed with Kewpie mayonnaise, which contains egg.
Sea bream from the Inland Sea. Served with soy sauce, which contains wheat.
Silky dashi-and-egg custard with things hidden in it — eaten with a spoon, hot. Dashi and soy.
Offered as a closer rather than a main event; pieces are generously sized and the rice is properly seasoned, which is not a given at an izakaya.
The shop's name literally means 'sake and food'. Rice-based, so gluten-free.

A breakfast kaiseki served at 08:30 on the third Sunday of the month only — a genuinely rare thing to be able to book in Japan, and the cheapest way into this kitchen. Reservation by phone, and 10% service is added on top.
From 12:00. Same price as dinner — this is a serious, expensive kitchen, not a cheap lunch. Prices move with the market, and 10% service is added.

From 18:00, by reservation only. The chef, Nakae Yuubun, cooked across Europe and the Middle East, then at a Tokyo ryotei and as head chef of Ginza Koju, and learned sake brewing at Okada Honke in Kako­gawa before opening here in 2019 — so expect Hyogo ingredients and a serious sake list. Kaiseki runs on dashi and soy and always includes fish; tell them well in advance about any restriction.

items.ja: 姫路おでん本舗盛り（5品）
items.note: The sampler, and the easiest possible introduction to Himeji oden — the counter is 30 seconds inside the JR station's souvenir hall, so you can do it between trains. Eat it with the ginger soy sauce on the counter, not mustard; that dip is what makes oden 'Himeji oden'. Run jointly with the Himeji Oden Cooperative and the city's sake brewers' association.
Cheapest oden in the city centre. Ingredients lean on Ieshima and Boze island seafood and other local produce. Broth is dashi plus soy sauce.

items.ja: 春夏秋冬限定おでんダネ
items.note: A rotating seasonal slot on top of the standing pot — worth asking what is in it today.

items.ja: 姫路の地酒のみ比べセット（3種）
items.en: Local sake tasting flight, three kinds
items.note: All seven Himeji-area breweries are poured here, which no other single counter in town does — the flight is the efficient way to find which one you like before buying a bottle in the same hall.
Contains barley.

items.ja: 本日の日替わりランチ
items.note: The reason this place is booked out at midday: a daily main, two starters, a mini pho, rice and a small dessert. The shop states plainly that the seasoning is tuned to Japanese palates, so it is milder than you might expect. Contains soy-based seasonings and fish sauce.

Indonesia's national fried rice, dark and sweet-savoury from kecap manis, served here with prawn crackers to scoop it up. Kecap manis is a wheat-containing sweet soy, and shrimp paste is standard — ask on both counts.

items.ja: 手羽先のインドネシア風唐揚げ～アヤムゴレン～
items.romaji: Tebasaki no Indoneshia-fu karaage — ayamu goren
items.en: Ayam goreng — Indonesian fried chicken wings
items.note: Wings steeped in a spice paste, then fried crisp, with sambal on the side. Sambal is the fiery Indonesian chilli relish; it often contains shrimp paste. Coating may be wheat flour.

items.ja: とろぉーりモッツァレラチーズのアジアンライスコロッケ
items.romaji: Torori mottsarera chiizu no ajian raisu korokke
items.note: Rice seasoned like nasi goreng, wrapped around cheese and fried, served with demi-glace — a fusion the shop invented. Breadcrumbed, so wheat.

items.ja: ホーチミンの生春巻き
items.romaji: Hoo Chi Min no nama harumaki
items.en: Ho Chi Minh fresh spring rolls (from 1 roll)
items.note: Prawn and vegetables in ultra-thin Vietnamese rice paper — not fried. Sold singly, so easy to try. Rice paper is gluten-free but the house miso dip is not.

items.ja: 牛肉のタイ風マリネ～ヤムヌア～
items.romaji: Gyuniku no Tai-fu marine — yamu nua
items.note: In Thailand this is brutally hot; the shop says it has dialled it down to gently spicy. Lime, beef, raw vegetables. Fish sauce.

items.ja: 甘海老とアボカドのタルタル～海老せん添え～
items.en: Sweet shrimp and avocado tartare with prawn crackers
items.note: Scoop it onto the crackers. Chilli mayonnaise contains egg.

items.ja: 三田ポークの冷しゃぶ～たっぷりパクチーのせ～
items.romaji: Sanda pooku no hiyashabu — tappuri pakuchii nose
items.en: Chilled Sanda pork shabu with coriander
items.note: Sanda pork is a Hyogo brand pig from the hills north of Kobe. Soy-milk sesame sauce.

items.ja: コリコリ中華くらげ～黒酢ソース～
items.note: Japanese jellyfish from the Ariake Sea — eaten for the squeaky, crunchy texture rather than flavour.

items.ja: タイ風海老と春雨のサラダ～ヤムウンセン～
items.romaji: Tai-fu ebi to harusame no sarada — yamu unsen
items.en: Yam woon sen — Thai glass noodle and prawn salad
items.note: Mung-bean glass noodles are gluten-free, but the dressing uses fish sauce and possibly soy.

items.ja: ピリ辛チャイニーズチキンと温泉玉子のバンバンジーサラダ
items.romaji: Pirikara chainiizu chikin to onsen tamago no banbanjii sarada
items.en: Bang bang chicken salad with soft-set egg
items.note: Steamed chicken marinated in Sichuan pepper and chilli oil; break the egg over it. Egg, and the sauce contains soy.

items.ja: タイ風海老すり身のトースト揚げ
items.romaji: Tai-fu ebi surimi no toosuto age
items.note: Prawn paste spread on bread and deep-fried. Wheat.

items.ja: 鶏皮のパリパリ揚げ～チリソース添え～
items.romaji: Torikawa no paripari age — chiri soosu zoe
items.en: Crisp-fried chicken skin with chilli sauce
items.note: Cheapest fried plate; Vietnamese hot chilli sauce on the side.

items.ja: プリプリ海老のチリマヨネーズ炒め
items.romaji: Puripuri ebi no chiri mayoneezu itame
items.note: The chef's declared signature. Egg in the mayonnaise; sauces usually contain soy.

items.ja: 金魚蘭特製の麻婆豆腐
items.note: Built on the shop's own malajiang chilli-and-Sichuan-pepper paste; the numbing sansho aroma is the point. Doubanjiang and soy contain wheat.

items.ja: 空芯菜のガーリック炒め（夏季）
items.note: Hollow-stemmed Vietnamese green, crunchy and mild. In winter the shop swaps in ta-sai, a slightly bitter Chinese brassica, at the same price. Usually finished with fish sauce or oyster sauce — ask.

items.ja: ベトナム風もちもち蒸し春巻き
items.note: Prawn and rice vermicelli in rice paper, steamed until chewy. Seasoning sauce may contain soy.

items.ja: とろとろ角煮の黒酢酢豚
items.en: Sweet-and-sour pork belly in black vinegar
items.note: Whole braised pork-belly blocks rather than small cubes. Battered and sauce-thickened, so wheat.

items.ja: 魚介とたっぷりの野菜のトムヤムクン
items.romaji: Gyokai to tappuri no yasai no tomu yamu kun
items.en: Tom yum kung with seafood and vegetables
items.note: Hot-and-sour Thai soup with prawn, squid and clams. Fish sauce and shrimp paste.

items.ja: 鶏肉と野菜のココナッツスープ～トムカーガイ～
items.romaji: Toriniku to yasai no kokonattsu suupu — tomu kaa gai
items.en: Tom kha gai — coconut chicken soup
items.note: Sour and mildly hot, smoothed with coconut milk. Fish sauce.
Flat rice noodles in clear broth — the noodles themselves are rice, so this is the most likely gluten-free option on the menu, but confirm the broth. Chilli sauce is added by you, not the kitchen.
Vegetable-loaded and light, but the broth is very unlikely to be meat-free — ask.
Tendon simmered to collapse.

items.ja: トムヤムクンのフォー
items.note: A Thai-Vietnamese hybrid the shop made up: rice noodles in hot-and-sour prawn soup.

items.ja: 肉そぼろのガパオのせご飯
items.romaji: Niku soboro no gapao nose gohan
items.en: Gapao — Thai basil minced chicken on rice
items.note: Minced chicken fried with chilli and holy basil over rice; add a soft-poached egg for ¥110. Fish sauce and oyster sauce.

items.ja: グリルチキンのグリーンカレー
items.note: Green chilli heat rounded off with coconut milk, over rice. A prawn version is ¥935, and red curry versions run the same prices. Curry pastes normally contain shrimp paste.

items.ja: ベトナム風焼きプリン
items.note: Firm baked caramel custard with a Vietnamese coffee sauce and condensed milk poured over. Egg and dairy.

items.ja: 金魚蘭のなめらか杏仁豆腐
items.note: Set almond-milk pudding, cool and barely sweet. Dairy.
Ripe banana and caramel in a fried wrapper with whipped cream. Wheat wrapper.

items.ja: ホットブレンドコーヒー
items.note: The teahouse sits at the castle's Otemon gate and is run by the city's machizukuri organisation, so prices are far below what a castle-gate café could charge. Open 10:00-17:00.
Black tea, not Japanese green tea.
Thick, sweet, non-alcoholic rice drink made from koji rather than sake lees — a winter warmer and a shrine-festival staple. Naturally sweet with no sugar added.
Dairy.
Whisked green tea with steamed milk. Dairy.
Dairy.
Dairy.
Dairy.
Comes unsweetened and black by default; syrup and milk are separate.
Unsweetened black tea over ice.
A local souvenir soda — 'cider' in Japan means clear lemonade, not apple. Bought as much for the bottle as the drink.
Yuzu is a fragrant Japanese citrus, sharper and more floral than lemon.
Wobbly translucent cubes dusted with roasted soybean flour and drizzled with black sugar syrup — cool, barely sweet, and about as traditional a castle-gate snack as exists. Cheapest thing here.
Almond butter on thick-cut toast is a Kansai kissaten habit, and Himeji sells its own almond butter as a souvenir. Wheat and dairy.

items.ja: アーモンドトースト・バニラ
items.en: Almond toast with vanilla ice cream
items.note: Hot toast with a scoop melting on top. Wheat and dairy.
Japanese hotcakes are thick, cakey and eaten with butter and syrup. Wheat, egg, dairy.
The classic thing to eat while walking back out through the gate. Cone contains wheat; dairy.
Espresso poured over ice cream. Dairy.
Iced coffee with a scoop of vanilla floating in it — a Showa-era café standard. Dairy.
Himeji's historic confection: a pale pink ball of bean paste shaped like a camellia bud, created for the Sakai lords of Himeji Castle. Usually contains egg white.
Flat crisp biscuits pressed to look like roof tiles and stamped with the castle — the standard Himeji gift. Wheat and egg.
Steamed buns of sweet bean paste with a faint salt edge. Wheat dough.
The spread from the toast, sold to take home. Dairy.

items.ja: バゲット（バジルバター付き）
items.note: The one thing regulars single out here — the basil butter more than the bread, and you can order extra baguette to finish the pasta sauce. The shop's own website is unreadable to modern browsers and it posts no menu online, so order by asking; the kitchen runs pizza, pasta and a lunch service, and the upstairs room seats about 25 for groups if you arrange it ahead. Wheat and dairy.
